questions.q: How do Fabric notebooks compare structurally to Databricks & Delta Lake's notebooks?
options: The exact same shape — a sequence of independently-runnable cells, one default language, magic commands overriding it per cell
Fabric notebooks don't support cells at all, only a single script
Fabric notebooks can only run SQL, never Python
Fabric notebooks require an entirely different execution model
questions.explain: This is directly the same concept from Databricks & Delta Lake Lesson 6, just in a different platform.

questions.q: What does attaching a Fabric notebook to a lakehouse do, compared to attaching to a Databricks cluster?
options: It has no effect on what code the notebook can run
Fabric provisions the Spark session automatically behind that attachment — no cluster configuration form to fill in at all
It only works for SQL cells, never PySpark cells
It requires the exact same VM-size and runtime configuration as Databricks
questions.explain: This is the real difference from Databricks & Delta Lake Lesson 4's compute-creation form.

questions.q: How does the attached lakehouse relate to spark.read.table("trips") resolving correctly?
options: Attachment has no effect on table resolution
spark.read.table() doesn't work in Fabric notebooks at all
The notebook already knows which lakehouse "trips" belongs to from the attachment, not from any path typed in code
The table name must always include the full lakehouse path explicitly
questions.explain: This mirrors Databricks & Delta Lake Lesson 16's spark.table() pattern, resolving via context rather than an explicit path.

questions.q: What's the relationship between Fabric's %%pyspark/%%sql and Databricks' %python/%sql?
options: Fabric only supports %%sql, never %%pyspark
Databricks' magic commands don't exist at all
They are completely unrelated magic command systems
Same underlying idea — overriding a cell's language — just different syntax: a double-percent cell-opening line instead of a single-percent inline prefix
questions.explain: The underlying concept is identical, even though the exact syntax differs between platforms.

questions.q: Do PySpark methods like filter, groupBy, and joins from Foundations' Chapter 4 work unchanged in a Fabric notebook?
options: No, Fabric requires an entirely different set of transformation methods
Yes — nothing about the DataFrame API itself is Fabric-specific; only the attachment step and magic command syntax differ
Only filter() works; groupBy() requires special Fabric-specific syntax
Only if the notebook is attached to a Databricks cluster instead of a lakehouse
questions.explain: This is the same point made throughout this course — the underlying PySpark skills transfer directly.
